blocks.content: When does using a control population in a undirectional selection experiment reduce the variance in response? Equation 18.30a, along with the coefficients from [[SEE_TABLE:18.7]], gives the expected variance with and without the use of a control. Assuming $ M = M_s = M_c $ and $ N = N_s = N_c $, this equation yields $$ \sigma^{2}\left[R_{C}(t)\right]_{control}-\sigma^{2}\left[R_{C}(t)\right]_{no control}=\left(\frac{t}{N}+\frac{1}{M_{0}}\right)h^{2}\sigma_{z}^{2}+\frac{1}{M}\sigma_{z}^{2}-\sigma_{b}^{2} $$

Assuming the between-line drift variance dominates (terms involving M can be ignored), the condition for the variance in response with a control to be larger than the response without one is approximately $$ t\sigma_{z}^{2}h^{2}/N>\sigma_{b}^{2} $$
